issues.failure_explanation: The three clauses on V are mutually incompatible under the standard reading of "supported in": supp V ⊂ Ω\Ω_int ⊂ Ω forces V = 0 on ∂Ω and on ℝ^d\Ω̄, so V cannot be strictly positive on a (ℝ^d-)neighbourhood of ∂Ω. Moreover, thm:LSW3 additionally requires V radial with V = 0 exactly for r ≤ R₁ and V′ ≥ 0 for all r, which forces V > 0 for every r > R₁; supp V is then unbounded and cannot be contained in the bounded set Ω\Ω_int, so thm:LSW3's hypotheses are unsatisfiable as literally stated. Finally, the proof of thm:nt_CAP needs φ = 1 on supp(1−χ) ⊇ ℝ^d\Ω while supp φ ⊂ {V ≥ a}, impossible whenever V = 0 outside Ω̄. All statements become simultaneously satisfiable only if "supported in Ω\Ω_int" is reinterpreted non-standardly as "V vanishes on Ω_int" with V > 0 on a two-sided neighbourhood of ∂Ω.

failure_location.quote: Let $V\in C^\infty(\Rea^d,\Rea)$ be non-negative, supported in $\Omega\setminus \Omega_{\rm int}$ and strictly positive in a neighbourhood of $\partial \Omega$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reword the conditions on V (e.g., V ∈ C^∞(ℝ^d), V = 0 on Ω̄_int, V ≥ v₀ > 0 on a neighbourhood of ∂Ω, dropping or reinterpreting "supported in Ω\Ω_int" as "vanishing on Ω_int"), noting that only V|_Ω enters the PDE; all results then hold under the forced reading.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's central object (the CAP potential) is inconsistently specified; taken literally, def:CAP describes an empty class (or thm:LSW3's hypothesis set is empty), which would render the decomposition theorem and all conditional FEM/GMRES results vacuous, and makes the cutoff construction in thm:nt_CAP's proof impossible.
issues.title: Incompatible specification of the CAP potential V
issues.why_classification: The intended object is unambiguous and the repair is a local rewording of one definition; under the forced reading no theorem's mathematical content is lost.
